title: Flattening a finite type quasi-coherent module by an admissible blowup
statement: Let $S$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism], let $f:X\to S$ be a quasi-compact morphism locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], and let $\mathcal F$ be a finite-type quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent], with finite presentation of module sheaves as in [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation]. Let $U\subseteq S$ be a quasi-compact open such that $\mathcal F|_{X_U}$ is of finite presentation and flat over $U$ (at every $x\in X_U$, its stalk is flat over $\mathcal O_{U,f(x)}$). Then there is a $U$-admissible blowup $S'\to S$ [def-nagata-admissible-blowup] such that the strict transform $\mathcal F'$ [def-trf-module-strict-transform] is flat over $S'$ and is of finite presentation as an $\mathcal O_{X\times_S S'}$-module.

source.place: Tag 0815, theorem-flatten-module (the module flattening theorem immediately preceding the scheme flattening lemma).

proof.text: Use strong induction on a natural strict upper bound d for all fibre-support dimensions. To prove the assertion at d, apply smooth affine reduction. For each n<d, its smooth-family premise follows from the smooth support induction step applied to the already established general assertion at n. The d=0 case has an empty range of n and hence requires no induction hypotheses.

The uniform fibre-dimension bound gives a natural d bounding the dimensions of all scheme fibres. Subspace monotonicity bounds each module fibre support by its fibre; thus d+1 is a strict upper bound. The induction yields an admissible blowup B with flat module strict transform F1.

The blowup permanence theorem makes the new base qcqs and F1 quasi-coherent of finite type. Properness makes the inverse image U1 compact. The quotient defining the transform becomes an isomorphism after restriction to U1. Its source is the restriction of the tensor pullback, identified by the open-square comparison with pullback of F|X_U. Tensor pullback preserves finite presentation, so F1 is finitely presented over U1. Convert finite-type ideal modules to finite-type ideal data by taking the image of their finite affine section modules in the structure sheaf. The ideal module is quasi-coherent as the kernel of the unit-to-closed-pushforward map: closed pushforward preserves quasi-coherence and kernels of quasi-coherent modules remain quasi-coherent.

The base-changed ambient morphism remains locally of finite presentation. Apply flatModulePresentationAfterBoundaryBlowup to F1 and U1. Choose a finite-type ideal cutting out the boundary and its admissible blowup C; the successive module transform is flat and finitely presented on the entire source.

Compose B and C by the module blowup calculus. Its support formula makes the composite centre disjoint from U, so it defines admissible data D. The comparison isomorphism identifies the successive transform with pullback of the single transform along the source isomorphism m over the base isomorphism e. Pull back by m inverse and use composition and identity pullback comparisons to identify with the single transform. Relative flatness transports through the inverse cartesian square; finite presentation transports by pullback and module isomorphism. Finally pass from affine-section relative flatness to the displayed stalk-flatness condition.
